introduction: On this Sunday, God asks through Isaiah, Can a woman forget her nursing child? Even if she should forget, I will not forget you. In the Gospel, Jesus tells us that we cannot serve both God and money, and that we should not be anxious, for our heavenly Father feeds the birds and clothes the lilies. Paul says that the Lord alone is our judge. Let us seek first the Kingdom of God.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, our souls rest in God alone. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may seek first God's Kingdom and his righteousness. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are anxious about food, clothing, work or money: that they may receive what they need and trust in God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who feel forgotten: that they may know that God will never forget them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who serve money above all: that they may find freedom in serving God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may live one day at a time, trusting our heavenly Father. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you feed the birds of the air and clothe the lilies of the field. Free us from anxiety, and help us seek first your Kingdom. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Seek first the Kingdom
reflection.body:
The people of Israel, in exile, feel abandoned: "The LORD has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me." God answers with one of the most tender images in the Bible: "Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb?" And he goes further: "Yes, these may forget, yet I will not forget you!" God's love is more faithful than even a mother's.

In the Gospel, Jesus begins with a clear choice: "No one can serve two masters... You can't serve both God and Mammon." Mammon means wealth, money treated as a master. We can use money, but we cannot let it rule us.

Then Jesus speaks to our anxieties: "don't be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear." He invites us to look at creation: "See the birds of the sky, that they don't sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren't you of much more value than they?" And: "Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow."

Jesus is not telling us to be careless or lazy. He is telling us that worry does not help: "Which of you by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?" And he gives us the right order of things: "But seek first God's Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well."

Finally, he teaches us to live one day at a time: "Therefore don't be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself."

The psalm expresses this trust: "My soul rests in God alone."

This week, notice what you are anxious about, and hand it over to God in prayer each morning. Take a moment to look at the birds or the flowers and remember that your Father cares for you. And ask what it would mean to put his Kingdom first.
